datafield.subfield: Second place winner in the 1st annual 2008 Student Artists' Book Competition at SCAD.
Pamphlet bound ultra suede cover with stitching. One of a kind.

"My significant other and I have been together for nearly six years. We have found it increasingly difficult to be together since we are from different countries; he is Canadian and I am American. We know that one of the easiest ways for us to stay together is through marriage but neither one of us is ready for that step in our lives, nor do we have access to the amount of funding it takes to create the wedding we want. When a Canadian citizen crosses the U.S. border with no particular visa they enter as a "visitor" and are granted a six-month period of time to stay here. So by leaving the U.S. and coming back within a short period of time, Jon, my partner, is again and again granted six months to remain here. The stamps acquired in our passports are visual proof of our resistance so this book represents a combined passport that symbolically suggests our journey together. I have made the size of this book similar to that of a passport. The cover is screen-printed with some text that I found during my research. The cover also has some decorative stitch work. These stitches are actually knots representing the 'tying the knot' in marriage. Each page has been stitched with red thread. This line represents the physical U.S./Canada border and it continues on each page, starting with the border of British Columbia and Alaska and ending with the border of Maine and New Brunswick. Numbers can be found on each page as well. These numbers represent the dates that our passports were stamped upon entering Canada and the US. On the back cover of the book there is a representation of the Canadian province of Nova Scotia. Although Nova Scotia does not border the U.S., it is significant for this book becasue it is where Jon is from and it is also where I lived and studied for three years." --Artist's statement.
